page: Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is a high-density compute and storage configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine provides 160 vCPUs across 80 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, supported by 320.0 GB of system memory at a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural element is the inclusion of 9,449 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The AMD processor includes hardware instruction support for AVX-512 vector computation, AVX-512 VNNI, BF16 operations, and cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI, running virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the D160alds_v7 in the top decile across nearly all compute and memory throughput tests. The host achieved a multi-core stress-ng metric of 287,625.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 29,391.0, accompanied by single-core scores of 3,791.58 and 2,883.0 respectively. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 463.49 GB/sec alongside 209.95 GB/sec in writes. Data processing throughput is demonstrated by 999.55 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, 83,957.0 in Clang compilation, 202.38 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 112.41 GB/sec in static web throughput.

Qualitatively, the D160alds_v7 offers high compute and storage density per deployed instance, though the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory provisioning represents an architectural tradeoff for environments requiring vast memory-to-core ratios. The dense 160-vCPU compute capacity and extensive direct-attached NVMe storage make it well positioned for large-scale build pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, batch ETL processing, CPU-based LLM inference, and distributed database nodes requiring rapid local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is a high-core compute and local-storage virtual machine delivering 160 vCPUs across 80 physical cores on a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 320.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 9,449 GB of fast bundled local NVMe SSD storage, the instance is engineered for parallel throughput without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile performance across raw compute, multi-threaded bzip3 compression, static web delivery, and caching engines, posting 202.38 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. With integrated support for AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, the D160alds_v7 provides strong resource density for compute-bound workloads, massive compilation farms, local NVMe-dependent databases, and intensive batch ETL pipelines.
